title: Hired for Gordon C. Harrison's hotel band in Texarkana
summary: Pianist Gordon C. Harrison, having heard of him through Little Rock musicians, sends a ticket and $35 a week to join his band at the new Grim Hotel.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And I played with Johnn Brown almost all of that summer, until the latter part of August. I was offered a job by a gentleman named Gordon C. Harrison, who was a great pianist, and he lived in Texacana, Texas. They were opening a new hotel in Texacana called the Grimm Hotel, and this hotel

was built right on the state line. It was a brand new, beautiful hotel. And Gordon C. Harrison had heard about me, and they sent me a ticket. And I left Johnnie Brown's band, and I went to Texicana. I called my mother and them up and told them I'd be through Little Rock that evening, and they came over to the railroad station to say hi to me. And the train must have spent about 15 minutes there, and I passed through Little Rock going to Texicana.

I arrived in Texicana and I joined this band. This was my first exposure to playing in a big, fine hotel where we had to play lunch -- luncheon music every day at noon, and dinner music every evening from 6:00 to 8:30.
Excuse me. You mentioned that this man had heard about you.

Yeah, he had heard about me, yes. He had heard about me through musicians who had played with the Royal City Band. You see, those communities are small communities, you know, see. Little Rock was only 140 miles -- less than 140 miles from Texicana. And he had organized this band with some musicians from Little Rock, and they knew me, see. And they recommended me to him, and he sent me a wire and he offered me a nice salary. I think the salary was $35.00 a week.
Had you developed into a soloist at this point?
Oh, yes. I was -- man, I was playing--
